```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

# Purpose

In the main comparisons Auto-ARIMA, ETS and Theta see only a store's own sales
history, while the tree models also see calendar, promotion and holiday
variables. A tree advantage could therefore come from the extra information
rather than from the model class. This file removes that difference: ARIMAX
and both boosted models receive exactly the same covariates, and every model
is evaluated on the same store-day rows.

# 1. Packages and data

```{r packages}
library(data.table)
library(forecast)
library(lightgbm)
library(xgboost)

# Same convention as the other stage files: train.csv and store.csv sit next
# to this file. A few other usual places are tried as a fallback.
data_dirs <- c(".", "..", "Data/rossmann-store-sales", "../Data/rossmann-store-sales")
DATA_DIR  <- data_dirs[file.exists(file.path(data_dirs, "train.csv"))][1]
if (is.na(DATA_DIR)) stop("train.csv not found in: ", paste(data_dirs, collapse = ", "))

SEED      <- 230923          # sampling and tree seeds
BOOT_SEED <- 230924          # bootstrap seed
H         <- 42              # forecast horizon in days
N_CORES   <- max(1, min(4, parallel::detectCores() - 1))
ORIGINS   <- as.Date(c("2015-05-08", "2015-06-19"))

dir.create("thesis_tables",    showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("rossmann_outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)

raw <- fread(file.path(DATA_DIR, "train.csv"))
raw[, Date := as.Date(Date)]
stores <- fread(file.path(DATA_DIR, "store.csv"))

cat("Data folder:", normalizePath(DATA_DIR), "\n")
cat("Installed versions: forecast", as.character(packageVersion("forecast")),
    "| lightgbm", as.character(packageVersion("lightgbm")),
    "| xgboost", as.character(packageVersion("xgboost")), "\n")
```

# 2. Store sample

The sample is fixed before any model is fitted. Only stores with a complete
daily record from 1 January 2013 up to the first origin are eligible, and this
is checked using data available at that origin only. Fifty stores are drawn,
stratified by store type (27 A, 1 B, 7 C, 15 D).

```{r sample}
set.seed(SEED)
eligible <- raw[Date <= ORIGINS[1], .(n = .N, first = min(Date)), by = Store]
full_len <- as.integer(ORIGINS[1] - as.Date("2013-01-01")) + 1
eligible <- eligible[n == full_len & first == as.Date("2013-01-01")]
pool <- merge(eligible, stores[, .(Store, StoreType)], by = "Store")

allocation <- c(a = 27L, b = 1L, c = 7L, d = 15L)
ids <- unlist(lapply(names(allocation), function(k)
  sample(sort(pool[StoreType == k, Store]), allocation[[k]])))

fwrite(pool[Store %in% ids], "rossmann_outputs/arimax_sample.csv")
cat("Eligible stores:", nrow(pool), "| sampled:", length(ids), "\n")
table(pool[Store %in% ids, StoreType])
```

# 3. Shared covariates

One design matrix is built once and used by every model: weekday indicators,
promotion and its weekday interactions, school and state holidays, opening
status, an annual sine/cosine pair and a linear time index.

```{r covariates}
raw <- raw[Store %in% ids][order(Store, Date)]
raw[, DOW := factor(as.integer(format(Date, "%u")), levels = 1:7)]
raw[, day := as.numeric(Date - as.Date("2013-01-01")) / 365.25]
raw[, annual_sin := sin(2 * pi * day)]
raw[, annual_cos := cos(2 * pi * day)]
raw[, holiday := as.integer(StateHoliday != "0")]

X <- model.matrix(~ DOW * Promo + SchoolHoliday + holiday + Open +
                    annual_sin + annual_cos + day, raw)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
colnames(X) <- make.names(colnames(X))
colnames(X)
```

# 4. Per-store Auto-ARIMA and ARIMAX

Each store gets its own model. Orders are chosen by AICc with a stepwise,
approximate search bounded by p, q ≤ 3, P, Q ≤ 1 and a maximum combined order
of 5, with weekly seasonality. For ARIMAX, regressor columns that are constant
or linearly dependent **in the training window** are dropped (a QR rank check
that never looks at test sales). Auto-ARIMA without regressors is the
within-experiment information ablation.

```{r arima-fns}
predict_store <- function(s, origin, use_x) {
  ix <- which(raw$Store == s & raw$Date <= origin)
  it <- which(raw$Store == s & raw$Date > origin & raw$Date <= origin + H)
  yy <- ts(raw$Sales[ix], frequency = 7)
  args <- list(y = yy, seasonal = TRUE, stepwise = TRUE, approximation = TRUE,
               max.p = 3, max.q = 3, max.P = 1, max.Q = 1, max.order = 5)
  keep <- integer()
  if (use_x) {
    xx <- X[ix, , drop = FALSE]
    qq <- qr(cbind(Intercept = 1, xx))
    keep <- sort(qq$pivot[seq_len(qq$rank)])
    keep <- keep[keep > 1] - 1L
    args$xreg <- xx[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  }
  fit  <- do.call(auto.arima, args)
  pred <- if (use_x) forecast(fit, xreg = X[it, keep, drop = FALSE], h = length(it))$mean
          else forecast(fit, h = length(it))$mean
  list(pred = data.table(Store = s, Date = raw$Date[it], Sales = raw$Sales[it],
                         Open = raw$Open[it], Prediction = as.numeric(pred)),
       order = paste(arimaorder(fit), collapse = ","),
       regressors = paste(colnames(X)[keep], collapse = ";"))
}
```

```{r arima-fits, cache=TRUE}
arima_pred <- list(); manifest <- list()
for (k in seq_along(ORIGINS)) {
  origin <- ORIGINS[k]
  for (use_x in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
    model <- if (use_x) "ARIMAX" else "Auto-ARIMA"
    fits <- parallel::mclapply(ids, function(s)
      tryCatch(predict_store(s, origin, use_x),
               error = function(e) list(error = conditionMessage(e), Store = s)),
      mc.cores = N_CORES)
    bad <- vapply(fits, function(z) !is.null(z$error), logical(1))
    # A failed store is an error, not a silent drop from the sample.
    if (any(bad)) { print(fits[bad]); stop("A store fit failed") }
    pp <- rbindlist(lapply(fits, `[[`, "pred"))
    pp[, `:=`(Model = model, Origin = origin)]
    arima_pred[[length(arima_pred) + 1]] <- pp
    manifest[[length(manifest) + 1]] <- data.table(
      Store = ids, Origin = origin, Model = model,
      Order = vapply(fits, `[[`, "", "order"),
      Regressors = vapply(fits, `[[`, "", "regressors"))
    cat(as.character(origin), model, "done\n")
  }
}
```

# 5. Pooled XGBoost and LightGBM, and the Store-DOW baseline

The trees are pooled across the 50 stores and get the same covariates plus
store indicator columns (so a store's level can be learned without splitting
on an ordinal store ID). The number of boosting rounds is chosen by early
stopping on the last 42 training days; the model is then refitted on the full
training window with that number of rounds. Capacity is fixed: depth 6 for
XGBoost, 31 leaves for LightGBM.

```{r tree-fns}
# xgboost < 2 (the server has 1.7.x) names the validation set `watchlist`;
# later releases call it `evals`. Pick whichever the installed version has.
xgb_fit_valid <- function(params, dtrain, dvalid) {
  a <- list(params = params, data = dtrain, nrounds = 1200,
            early_stopping_rounds = 50, verbose = 0)
  if ("evals" %in% names(formals(xgb.train))) a$evals <- list(valid = dvalid)
  else a$watchlist <- list(valid = dvalid)
  do.call(xgb.train, a)
}
# 1.7.x keeps a one-based $best_iteration; later releases only keep the
# zero-based booster attribute.
xgb_best <- function(fit) {
  b <- tryCatch(as.integer(fit$best_iteration), error = function(e) integer())
  if (!length(b) || is.na(b)) b <- as.integer(xgb.attr(fit, "best_iteration")) + 1L
  b
}
```

```{r tree-fits, cache=TRUE}
tree_pred <- list(); rounds <- list()
storex <- model.matrix(~ factor(Store) - 1, raw)
xx <- cbind(X, storex)
for (k in seq_along(ORIGINS)) {
  origin <- ORIGINS[k]
  ix <- which(raw$Date <= origin)
  it <- which(raw$Date > origin & raw$Date <= origin + H)
  trainx <- xx[ix, , drop = FALSE]; yy <- raw$Sales[ix]
  vv <- which(raw$Date[ix] > origin - H)      # last 42 training days
  tt <- setdiff(seq_along(ix), vv)

  # LightGBM
  lp_par <- list(objective = "regression", metric = "rmse", num_leaves = 31,
                 learning_rate = .05, min_data_in_leaf = 20, num_threads = 4,
                 seed = SEED, verbosity = -1, deterministic = TRUE,
                 force_col_wise = TRUE)
  lv  <- lgb.train(lp_par, lgb.Dataset(trainx[tt, ], label = yy[tt]), nrounds = 1200,
                   valids = list(valid = lgb.Dataset(trainx[vv, ], label = yy[vv])),
                   early_stopping_rounds = 50, verbose = -1)
  lfit <- lgb.train(lp_par, lgb.Dataset(trainx, label = yy), nrounds = lv$best_iter, verbose = -1)
  lp <- predict(lfit, xx[it, , drop = FALSE])

  # XGBoost
  xp_par <- list(objective = "reg:squarederror", eta = .05, max_depth = 6,
                 nthread = 4, seed = SEED)
  xv   <- xgb_fit_valid(xp_par, xgb.DMatrix(trainx[tt, ], label = yy[tt]),
                        xgb.DMatrix(trainx[vv, ], label = yy[vv]))
  bx   <- xgb_best(xv); stopifnot(length(bx) == 1, !is.na(bx))
  xfit <- xgb.train(xp_par, xgb.DMatrix(trainx, label = yy), nrounds = bx, verbose = 0)
  xpred <- predict(xfit, xgb.DMatrix(xx[it, , drop = FALSE]))

  rounds[[k]] <- data.table(Origin = origin, LightGBM = lv$best_iter, XGBoost = bx)

  for (model in c("LightGBM", "XGBoost", "Store-DOW")) {
    pp <- copy(raw[it, .(Store, Date, Sales, Open)])
    if (model == "Store-DOW") {
      # Mean open-day sales per store and weekday over the training window.
      bm <- raw[Date <= origin & Open == 1 & Sales > 0,
                .(Prediction = mean(Sales)), by = .(Store, DOW)]
      pp[, DOW := raw$DOW[it]]
      pp <- merge(pp, bm, by = c("Store", "DOW"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
      pp[, DOW := NULL]
    } else pp[, Prediction := if (model == "LightGBM") lp else xpred]
    pp[, `:=`(Model = model, Origin = origin)]
    tree_pred[[length(tree_pred) + 1]] <- pp
  }
  cat(as.character(origin), "trees and baseline done\n")
}
rbindlist(rounds)
```

# 6. Accuracy on identical rows

All models are scored on the same open, positive-sales store-days. The
checks stop the knit if any forecast is missing or if the models at one
origin were not evaluated on the same number of rows.

```{r accuracy}
allpred <- rbindlist(c(arima_pred, tree_pred), use.names = TRUE)
fwrite(allpred, "rossmann_outputs/arimax_predictions.csv")
fwrite(rbindlist(manifest), "rossmann_outputs/arimax_model_manifest.csv")

pred <- allpred[Open == 1 & Sales > 0]
stopifnot(!anyNA(pred$Prediction))
counts <- pred[, .N, by = .(Origin, Model)]
stopifnot(all(counts[, .(same = uniqueN(N) == 1), by = Origin]$same))

res <- pred[, .(RMSE = sqrt(mean((Sales - Prediction)^2)),
                MAE  = mean(abs(Sales - Prediction)),
                N = .N, Stores = uniqueN(Store)), by = .(Origin, Model)]
fwrite(res, "thesis_tables/arimax_comparison.csv")
res
```

# 7. Paired block-bootstrap intervals

For each origin, ARIMAX is compared with Auto-ARIMA, XGBoost and LightGBM.
The statistic is comparator MSE minus ARIMAX MSE, so a positive value favours
ARIMAX. Daily pooled squared losses are resampled in circular blocks of seven
days (six blocks cover the 42-day holdout), 2000 times. Resampling whole days
keeps the dependence across stores on the same day, and seven-day blocks keep
the weekly pattern.

```{r bootstrap}
daily <- pred[, .(SSE = sum((Sales - Prediction)^2), N = .N), by = .(Origin, Model, Date)]
set.seed(BOOT_SEED)
ci <- list()
for (k in seq_along(ORIGINS)) for (m in c("Auto-ARIMA", "XGBoost", "LightGBM")) {
  o <- ORIGINS[k]
  a <- daily[Origin == o & Model == "ARIMAX"][order(Date)]
  b <- daily[Origin == o & Model == m][order(Date)]
  stopifnot(identical(a$Date, b$Date), identical(a$N, b$N), nrow(a) == H)
  boot <- replicate(2000, {
    starts <- sample.int(H, H / 7, TRUE)
    j <- unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) ((s - 1 + 0:6) %% H) + 1))
    sum(b$SSE[j] - a$SSE[j]) / sum(a$N[j])
  })
  q <- quantile(boot, c(.025, .975))
  ci[[length(ci) + 1]] <- data.table(
    Origin = o, Comparison = paste(m, "minus ARIMAX"),
    MSE_difference = sum(b$SSE - a$SSE) / sum(a$N), Lower = q[1], Upper = q[2])
}
ci <- rbindlist(ci)
fwrite(ci, "thesis_tables/arimax_uncertainty.csv")

# How the thesis text will read each interval.
ci[, Reading := fifelse(Lower > 0, "favours ARIMAX",
                fifelse(Upper < 0, "favours comparator", "includes zero"))]
ci
```
